title: Case, mid designer, weak answers, tough

questions.text: PanTrail is a meal-kit app. New users often stop before they finish setting up their first weekly box. How would you approach improving that?
You have three ideas: a taste quiz, a recipe preview and one-tap reorder. Which first and why?
PanTrail wants a feature for people who cook for one. What do you recommend?
Estimate how many users start setup each day if PanTrail gets 1 million installs a year.
How would you decide whether to redesign the whole home screen?
How would you explain the value of a design change to a business owner?

persona.pushback_style: asks why not the simpler option

brief.curveball: Tell the candidate the design team just lost half its time this month and one of the three launch features must be cut.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Mira, I'm Victor, a design lead. This is a thirty minute product case. I will push on your answers, so do not take it personally.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Victor. Okay, that is fine.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Where are you joining from?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: From my apartment. It is quiet.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: I will give you three cases. Talk through your thinking. We will leave a few minutes at the end for questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: PanTrail is a meal-kit app. New users often stop before they finish setting up their first weekly box. How would you approach improving that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would make the setup shorter. Fewer steps is better. Maybe add some nice pictures and a progress bar so people feel good.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Which step do users leave at, and how would you find out?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think probably the payment step. People do not like paying. I would maybe ask users what they think.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Who are these users, and what do they want from their first box?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Busy people who want to cook at home. They want simple recipes. So I would show those first, and check how many finish setup after we change it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: You have three ideas: a taste quiz, a recipe preview and one-tap reorder. Which first and why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would do the taste quiz first because it is more personal. Users like personal things. The others are also good but the quiz is the best.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why not one-tap reorder? It is the simpler option and costs less.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Reorder only works for people who already ordered. New users have nothing to reorder, so the quiz helps more at the start. But reorder is cheaper, so maybe it is good later.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: PanTrail wants a feature for people who cook for one. What do you recommend?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would add smaller portions. People who cook for one want less food. And maybe a lower price.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: New fact. The design team just lost half its time this month, and one of your three launch features must be cut. What do you do?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would talk to the team and see what is possible. Maybe we cut something small. I am not sure which one.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is the end of the cases. Do you have questions for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What does a typical week look like on your team?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Two design reviews, one user test, and a lot of time with product managers and engineers.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is our time, Mira. The recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Victor.

notes: Weak for mid: generic answers, no numbers, no recommendation. Pushback and curveball included.
